newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Demand for Nigerian oil shares lifts bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Demand for Nigerian oil shares lifts bourse index.

text.p: The Nigerian stock market ended confidently on Thursday as an undiminished appetite for oil shares buoyed the index, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 6,971.39 from 6,957.48 on Wednesday.
"As Christmas approaches many traders are hoping to stumble on oil company shares from willing sellers in need of cash," one analyst said.
Agip, National Oil and Mobil rose 50 kobo each to 23.12 naira, 46.50 naira and 49.50 naira respectively. African Petroleum gained 20 kobo to 44.50 naira.
Unipetrol finished 30 kobo higher at 57.50 naira. Total added 20 kobo to 57.00 naira.

Union Bank, was on the move upward again, closing at 5.50 naira on renewed demand. Nestle Foods gained 50 kobo to close at 48.65 naira. West African Portland Cement Company closed 20 kobo higher at 45.30 naira.
Nigerian Tobacco Company dropped 15 kobo to 3.20 naira in the absence of investor interest.
Conglomerate Lever Brothers fell 10 kobo to 20.50 naira. UAC was 10 kobo lower at 7.30 naira and CFAO dropped three kobo to 2.50 naira.
Nigerian Breweries fell five kobo aon Thursday to end at 19.45 naira.
